P: Godhūma，wheat （usually mentioned with yava，spelt） Miln.267； DA.I，163； SnA 323．See dhañña．（Page 255）
DOP: go m.f. [ ts ] ( sg. nom. go; acc. gavaṃ, gāvuṃ, gaṃ; dat./gen. gavassa 1 ; abl. gavā; loc. gave; pl. nom. gāvo, gavā; acc. gāvo; instr. gohi; gen. gavaṃ, gunnaṃ; loc. gosu; see also Sadd 209, 6 foll. ; 214, 32 foll. ; iic go- and, esp. before initial vowel, gava 1 - qv ; ifc -gava 1 , -gu 3 , -go); 1. ( m. ) an ox ; ( f. ) a cow ; ( pl. ) cattle ; Abh 495 (goṇo go vasabho vuso); 498 (gāvī ca siṅginī go ca); 869 (go pumitthiyaṃ); Vin I 150, 9 (gāvuṃ vā te demi gāviṃ vā te demi); D I 201, 25 (gavā khīraṃ khīramhi dadhi …); M I 429, 32 (yadi vā gavassa yadi vā mahisassa …); S I 6, 9* (gomiko gohi tath’ eva nandati) = Sn 33; S I 221, 34* (ajjhārūhati dummedho go va bhiyyo palāyinaṃ); IV 181, 12 foll. (tena hi tvaṃ Nanda sāmikānaṃ gāvo niyyādehī ti, gamissanti bhante gāvo vacchagiddhiniyo ti); A I 162, 12* (gosu pārevatāsu vā); II 42, 16 (yathārūpe … yaññe gāvo haññanti); 75, 33* (gunnaṃ ce taramānānaṃ jimhaṃ gacchati puṅgavo sabbā tā jiṃhaṃ gacchanti) ≠ Ja III 111, 17* (gavaṃ ce taramānānaṃ); Sn 296 (gāvo no paramā mittā yāsu jāyanti osadhā); 310 (adhammo iti pakkanduṃ yaṃ satthaṃ nipatī gave; Pj II 323, 33 : yasmā gāvimhi satthaṃ nipatī ti vuttaṃ hoti); 580 (ekameko va maccānaṃ go vajjho viya niyyati); Ja I 336, 11* (usabhā rukkhā gāviyo gavā ca); II 428, 19* (ahaṃ gāmavaraṃ icche brāhmaṇī ca gavaṃ sataṃ); IV 481, 12* (gavaṃ va naṭṭhaṃ puriso yathā vane pariyesatī); V 15, 27* (āhiṇḍatī go-r-iva bhakkhasādī; 18, 21´ : go-r-ivā ti goṇo viya); Cp 1:9:26 (datvā dāsidāsaṃ gavaṃ dhanaṃ; Cp-a 85, 20 : gavan ti dhenuṃ); Mil 267, 21 (atthi hatthī assā gāvo mahisā …); Vism 166, 33 (gopo ekasmiṃ vaje sabbā gāvo samāharati); — ifc see kūṭago ( sv kūṭa 2 ), dammago ( sv dammati ), paṭṭhitago ( sv paṭṭhita ); — see also cittagu ( sv citta 2 ), jaraggava ( sv jara 1 ), tiṭṭhagu, digu ( sv dvi ); — 2. ( m. ) an organ of sense ; Sadd 241, 13* (go goṇe c’ indriye … vattate); 241, 18 (gāvo cakkhādīn’ indriyāni caranti etthā ti gocaro); — 3. ( m. ) the earth ; Abh 181 (vasumatī go ku); Sadd 241, 13* (go … bhumyaṃ … vattate); Ps III 435, 29 (go ti hi paṭhaviyā nāmaṃ); — 4. ( m. ) speech; under-standing ; Sadd 241, 13* (go … vacane c’ eva buddhiyaṃ … vattate); 241, 28 foll. (ten’ āhu porāṇā gan tāyatī ti gottaṃ, Gotamo ti hi pavattamānaṃ gaṃ vacanaṃ buddhiṃ ca tāyati ekaṃsikavisayatāya rakkhatī ti gottaṃ); — 5. ( m. ) the sun ; Sadd 241, 14* (go … ādicce … vattate); 242, 12 (gosaddo ādicce vattati gogottaṃ Gotamaṃ name ti); — 6. ( m. ) a ray of light ; Sadd 241, 14* (go … rasmiyaṃ … vattate); 242, 21 (uṇhā gāvo rasmiyo etassā ti uṇhagu suriyo); — see also uṇhagu ( sv uṇha ); — 7. ( m. ) water ; Sadd 241, 14* (go … pānīye pi ca vattate); 242, 24 (gosītacandanan ti … gosaddena hi jalaṃ vuccati, go viya sītaṃ candanaṃ); — °- kaṇṭaka , m. [go + kaṇṭaka 1 ], 1. a plant, SAF: small caltrops, Turkey blossom, Tribulus terrestris L. ; Abh 583 (~o ca siṅghāṭo); — 2. a sharp clod churned up by cattle ; Kkh 2 151, 24 ; Sp 756, 18 (~o nāma gāvīnaṃ khuracchinnakaddamo vuccati); 1088, 4 (te kira ~e ekapaṭalikā upāhanā rakkhituṃ na sakkonti); — ~-hata, mfn. , churned into sharp clods by cattle ; Vin I 195, 37 (kaṇhuttarā bhūmi kharā ~-hatā) ≠ A I 136, 32 (Mp II 225, 11 foll. : navavaṭṭhe deve gāvīhi akkantakkantaṭṭhāne khurantarehi kaddamo uggantvā tiṭṭhati, so vātātapena sukkho kakacadantasadiso hoti dukkhasamphasso … gunnaṃ khurantarehi chinnā ti pi attho); — °- kaṇṇa , m. , 1. a span ; Abh 267; — 2. a kind of deer or elk ; Abh 612 (~o gaṇikaṇṭakā); Ja III 75, 22 (eko sūkaro eko ~o eko mahiso eko gavayo …); V 406, 30´ (gaṇino ti ~ā); Ps I 120, 9 ( in cpd ); Ap-a 536, 10* ; — gokaṇṇā [ti] in Ee at Sv 834, 20 is wr for gokāṇā qv ; — °- kaṇṇaka , m. , a kind of arrow ;? a spike ;? Mhv 76:48 (tikkhagge vāraṇatthāya vāraṇānaṃ ayomaye ~e nekasatasahassagaṇite; vl gokaṇṭake); — °- kāṇā , f. [go + kāṇa 1 ], a cow blind in one eye ; D III 38, 14 foll. ( Be, Ee, Se so; Ce go kāṇā; Sv 834, 20 : ~ā ti ekakkhihatā kāṇā gāvī, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee wr gokaṇṇā ti); 53, 18 (~aṃ pariyantacāriniṃ karotha); — °- kula , n. , a cattle-shed; a cow-pen ; Abh 190 (goṭṭhaṃ tu ~aṃ vajo); S IV 289, 5 (adhivāsentu me therā svātanāya ~e bhattan ti); Ja VI 297, 18´ ; — °- khāyitaka , mfn. , (to be) grazed by cattle ; Vism 415, 3 (sassesu pana ~-mattesu jātesu; Vism-mhṭ [ Be ] II 50, 22 : gohi khāditabbappamāṇesu) = Paṭis-a 368, 12 ( Be, Ce so; Ee, Se °-khāyitamattesu); Sadd 327, 20 ; — °- gavesa , mfn. , searching for cattle ; Ja V 70, 1* (eko caraṃ ~o mūḷho accasariṃ vane; 72, 13´ : naṭṭhagoṇe gavesanto); — °- ghaṃsikā , f. , a “cow-rubber”? a roller, a rod ; Vin II 117, 30 (kaṭhinaṃ paribhijjati, anujānāmi bhikkhave ~āya kaṭhinaṃ saṅgharitun ti kaṭhinaṃ viveṭhiyati …; Sp 1207, 3 : ~āyā ti veḷuṃ vā rukkhadaṇḍakaṃ vā anto katvā tena saddhiṃ saṅgharitun ti attho); — °- ghātaka , m. [go + ghātaka 1 ], one who kills cows, a butcher ; Vin III 105, 30 (Sp 508, 13 : ~o ti gāvo vadhitvā vadhitvā aṭṭhito maṃsaṃ mocetvā vikkiṇitvā jīvikaṃ kappanakasatto); D II 294, 18 ; A III 302, 15 ; Ja V 270, 4* (corā ~ā luddā); Vism 348, 14 ; — °- ghātana , n. , cattle-killing, cow-slaughter ; Pj II 323, 25 (taṃ ~aṃ disvā, Ce, Ee so; Be, Se °-ghātakaṃ); — °- cara , m. [ cf S., BHS gocara] 1. grazing; a search for food; where and on what animals feed; the particular feeding-ground, the particular food of an animal ; Vin III 147, 31 (mahā sakuṇasaṅgho tasmiṃ pallale divasaṃ ~aṃ caritvā); D III 23, 22 (tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ naditvā ~āya pakkameyyaṃ; Sv 827, 14 : āhāratthāya pakkameyyaṃ); Dhp 135 (yathā daṇḍena gopālo gāvo pacceti ~aṃ); Sn 39 (migo … yenicchakaṃ gacchati ~āya); Ja I 221, 31 (imasmiṃ sare udakaṃ parittaṃ ~o ca mando nidāgho ca mahanto); III 26, 2 (ekassa sīhassa … galo uddhumāyi, ~aṃ gaṇhituṃ na sakkoti); 52, 1 (attano ~-ṭṭhāne ~aṃ gahetvā); Mil 393, 14 (biḷāro āsanne yeva ~aṃ pariyesati); Ps I 117, 9 (jaraggavo divā ~e caritvā); Vv-a 218, 31 foll. (gāvo caranti etthā ti ~o, ~o viyā ti ~o ghāsesanaṭṭhānaṃ); Moh 167, 8 foll. (gāvo caranti etthā ti ~o gunnaṃ caraṇaṭṭhānaṃ, taṃsadisatāya pana sabbo pi pavattivisayo ~o ti veditabbo); Mhv 19:73 (rañño maṅgalahatthī … aṭṭhāsi ~aṃ caraṃ); — ifc see vana- ( sv vana 1 ), vāri-; — 2. a bhikkhu ’s begging-round; where bhikkhu s (properly) beg for food ; Vin II 208, 22 (~o pucchitabbo agocaro pucchitabbo; Sp 1281, 5 : gocaragāmo āsanne udāhu dūre …); Pv 36:43 (addasā samaṇaṃ … paṭikkantaṃ ~ato nivattaṃ; Pv-a 240, 22 : piṇḍapātapaṭikkantaṃ, ten’ āha ~ato nivattan ti); Thī 427 (ayyā Jinadattā āgacchi ~āya caramānā; Thī-a 247, 28 : ~āyā ti bhikkhāya); Ap 294, 20 ; Vibh 247, 11 foll. ; Sp 788, 3 (vesiyādi-agocaraṃ pahāya saddhāsampannakulādinā ca ~ena sampanno); Nidd-a I 451, 1 (~o ti piṇḍapātādīnaṃ atthāya upasaṅkamituṃ yuttaṭṭhānaṃ); — ifc see ācāra-, mahā- (s v maha[t]), vesiyā-; — ~-gāma, m. , the village where bhikkhu s or other ascetics beg for food; a village where bhikkhu s can (properly) beg for food ; M I 167, 6 ; Ja IV 8, 9 (ekaṃ indavāruṇikarukkhaṃ ~-gāmaṃ katvā); Vism 97, 29 (mettā bhāvetabbā … ~-gāmamhi issarajane); Sp 285, 16 ; 1267, 2 (amhākaṃ ~-gāme piṇḍāya caritvā); Ps II 174, 4 (sampattapabbajitānaṃ sulabhapiṇḍaṃ ~-gāmaṃ ca addasaṃ); Pv-a 12, 18 (sundaro ’yaṃ ~-gāmo manussā ca saddhāsampannā paṇītaṃ piṇḍa-pātaṃ denti …); — 3. ( i ) where the mind (properly) ranges and finds sustenance; a field or scope or sphere of action or attention ; D III 58, 19 (~e bhikkhave caratha sake pettike visaye; Sv 846, 20 : ~e ti carituṃ yuttaṭṭhāne); S V 148, 1 (ko ca bhikkhave bhikkhuno ~o sako pettiko visayo, yad idaṃ cattāro satipaṭṭhānā); Dhp 22 (paṇḍitā appamāde pamodanti ariyānaṃ ~e ratā); 93 (suññato animitto ca vimokho yassa ~o) = Th 92; Sn 961 (kyāss’ assu idha ~ā); Th 1085 (accheraṃ vata buddhānaṃ gambhīro ~o sako); Ap 48, 10 (vinayo mayhaṃ ~o); Paṭis I 180, 6 (~aṃ ca pajānāti; Paṭis-a 512, 27 : ~an ti vipassanākhaṇe saṅkhārārammaṇaṃ, maggakkhaṇe ca phalakkhaṇe ca nibbānārammaṇaṃ); II 150, 13 (ime panca dhammā dhammapaṭisambhidāya ārammaṇā c’ eva honti ~ā ca); Vism 19, 16 (~o pana tividho upanissayagocaro ārakkhagocaro upanibandhagocaro ti); Sv 465, 15 (paṭibhaṃsū ti paṭibhāṇasaṅkhātassa ñāṇassa ~ā ahesuṃ); Paṭis-a 232, 30 (samādhissa ~esu kasiṇādīsu ārammaṇesu … chekabhāvo); — ifc see ārakkha-, upanibandha-, upanissaya-; — ~’-ajjhatta, ( mf ) n. , what is internal as the scope of action or attention; a sphere of attention within oneself ;? Spk III 206, 4 (~’-ajjhatte pavattāya satiyā); It-a II 168, 10 (ajjhattarato samāhito ti evamādisu vuttaṃ idaṃ ~’-ajjhattaṃ nāma); Th-a III 167, 6 (~’-ajjhatte suṭṭhu samāhitā hutvā); — ( ii ) the range of the organs of sense; an object of sense ; Abh 94 (rūpaṃ saddo gandharasā phasso dhammo ca ~ā); Kv 252, 17 (maṃsacakkhussa visayo ānubhāvo ~o); Sv 224, 15 (āruppe pana dibbacakkhussa ~o n’ atthī ti); Vibh-a 47, 14 (cakkhādīnaṃ pana ~-ttā); — agocara, m. 1. not the proper feeding-ground; an unsuitable feeding-ground (for a particular animal) ; Ja II 40, 14 (imaṃ ṭhānaṃ tava agocaro); 60, 2 (tiracchānagatā pi agocare carantā sapattahatthaṃ gacchanti); Pj II 39, 15 (tā gāvo agocaraṃ pariharitvā gocare cāretvā); — 2. an unsuitable place for bhikkhu s to beg, an unsuitable person for bhikkhu s to beg from ; Vin II 208, 22 (Sp 1281, 7 : agocaro nāma micchādiṭṭhikānaṃ vā gāmo paricchinnabhikkho vā gāmo); M I 11, 2 (yathārūpe anāsane nisinnaṃ yathārūpe agocare carantaṃ …; Ps I 80, 32 : ayutto gocaro agocaro, so vesiyādibhedo pañca-vidho); Nidd I 473, 8 foll. (Nidd-a I 451, 2 : ayuttaṭṭhānaṃ agocaro) ≠ Vibh 246, 38 foll. ; Pj I 237, 2 (chabbidhe ca agocare carati, seyyathīdaṃ vesiyagocare vidhavathulla-kumārikapaṇḍakabhikkhunīpānāgāragocare ti); — 3. not being within the range (of), not a field or scope or sphere of action or attention; where the mind should not range or find sustenance; an unsuitable field of action or attention ; S V 147, 16 foll. (mā agocare carittha paravisaye … ko ca bhikkhave bhikkhuno agocaro paravisayo, yad idaṃ pañca kāmaguṇā); Ja VI 438, 32 (agocaro esa mayhaṃ gahapatisippam evāhaṃ jānāmi); Pj I 246, 9 (aṇukā ti maṃsacakkhussa agocarā dibbacakkhuvisayā); Ud-a 319, 8 (vācāya agocaraṃ ariyānaṃ kathāya avisayaṃ musāvādaṃ bhaṇantī ti); 321, 29 ([maccurājassa] adassanaṃ agocaraṃ gaccheyya); — sagocara, mfn. , having the same feeding-ground or sphere of action ; Ja II 31, 25* (Suhanu pi tādiso yeva yo Soṇassa sagocaro; 32, 8´ foll. : yath’ eva hi Soṇo assagocaro asse ḍasanto carati tathā Suhanu pi, iminā nesaṃ samānagocarataṃ dasseti); — °- caraṇatthāya in Ee at Ja VI 335, 10´ is prob. wr; Be, Se gocaratthāya; Ce caraṇatthāya; — °- cari , °- carika , °- cariya 1 , m. , one of the types of elephant (the lowest) ; Ja IV 234, 12´ (gocariyādīni aṭṭha hatthikulāni abhibhavitvā atikkamitvā uposathakule jāto); V 418, 13´ (gocarikādi-bhedena dasavidhena nāgakulena, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be gocariyādi-); Sv 573, 16* foll. (gocari kalambo gaṅgeyyo … yaṃ dasannaṃ gocarisaṅkhātānaṃ pakat-ihatthīnaṃ balaṃ taṃ ekassa kalambassā ti); Ps II 6, 20 (chaddanto nāgarājā na gocariyahatthikulādisu navasu kulesu uppajjati chaddantakule yeva uppajjati); — see also kāḷāvaka; — °- cariya 2 , mfn. [ cf BHS gocarika], (according to cts) of a reddish or brownish colour ;? Vin III 226, 25 (navaṃ pana bhikkhunā santhataṃ kārayamānena dve bhāgā suddhakāḷakānaṃ eḷakalomānaṃ ādātabbā tatiyaṃ odātānaṃ catutthaṃ ~ānaṃ; Sp 684, 21 : ~ānan ti kapilavaṇṇānaṃ); V 36, 1 ; — °- ṭṭha ( and guṭṭha ?), m.n. , a cow-pen; a cattle-fold ; Abh 190 (~aṃ tu gokulaṃ vajo); M I 79, 14 (ye te ~ā paṭṭhitagāvo apagatagopālakā; Ps II 47, 1 : ~ā ti govajā); II 186, 2 (brāhmaṇo bahi nagare gāvo ~e dohāpeti); Ja IV 223, 7* (~aṃ majjaṃ … ārakā parivajjehi, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se guṭṭhaṃ; 223, 22´ foll. : ~aṃ majjaṃ kirāṭan ti ayaṃ potthakesu pāṭho, aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana ~aṃ majjaṃ kirāsaṃ cā ti vatvā ~an ti gunnaṃ ṭhitaṭṭhānaṃ, Be so; Ce guṭṭhamajjaṃ kirāsaṃ cā ti ayaṃ potthakesu pāṭho …; Se guṭṭhaṃ majjaṃ kirāsaṃ cā ti ayaṃ potthakesu pāṭho …; Ee guṭṭhimacchaṃ gharāsavā ti ayaṃ potthakesu pāṭho aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana goṭṭhimajjakirāsavā ti vatvā goṭṭhin ti gunnaṃ ṭhitaṭṭhānaṃ, prob. wr ); Bv-a 264, 15 (yathā usabho ~aṃ bhinditvā yathāsukhaṃ icchitaṭṭhānaṃ pāpuṇāti); — ~-phala, n. pn: Godhāvarī. A canal, built by Parakkamabāhu I., connecting the Kāragaṅgā and the Parakkamasāgara (Cv.lxxix.57).

Godhāvarī (v.l. Godāvari). A river in Dakkhiṇāpatha, of which it forms the southern boundary. During the Buddha’s time, the Aḷaka (or Mulaka) king and the Assaka king (both Andhakas) had settlements on its northern bank, and Bāvarī’s hermitage lay in the territory between their dominions (Snp.vs.977). The Commentary (Snp-a.ii.581) says that near this spot the Godhāvarī divided into two branches, forming an island three leagues in extent, and the island was a dense forest, known as the Kapiṭṭhavana. Bāvarī’s hermitage occupied a region of five leagues. In the past this region had been the abode of various sages, such as Sarabhaṅga (Ja.v.132, 136; Mvu.i.363). According to the Aṅguttara Commentary (AN-a.i.182), Bāvarī’s hermitage was on a bend of the river (Godhāvarīvaṅke). The Godhāvarī is one of the holiest rivers in Southern India, rising in Brahmagiri near the village of Triyanvaka and sanctified by its connection with Rāma and various saints.

pn: Godhajātaka 01. (Ja 138). The Bodhisatta was once born as a lizard and paid homage to a good ascetic living near the ant-hill where he dwelt. The good ascetic left and was replaced by a wicked one, to whom the Bodhisatta paid like homage. One day, the villagers brought a dish of lizard’s flesh to the ascetic. Being attracted by its flavour, he planned to kill the Bodhisatta, that he might have more of the flesh. But the Bodhisatta discovered his intention just in time, and, making good his escape, denounced the hypocrite. The story was told in reference to a wicked monk. Ja.i.480f.

Godhajātaka 02. (Ja 141). The Bodhisatta was born once as an iguana, leader of many others. His son became intimate with a young chameleon, whom he used to clip and embrace. The Bodhisatta warned his son against this unnatural intimacy, but, finding his advice of no avail, and knowing that danger would come to them through the chameleon, he prepared a way of escape, should the need arise. The chameleon, growing tired of the friendship with the iguana, showed a trapper the home of the iguanas. The trapper made a fire round the hole and killed many of the iguanas as they tried to escape, but the Bodhisatta reached safety through the hole he had provided.

The story was told about a treacherous monk, identified with the young iguana (Ja.i.487f). For details see the Mahilāmukhajātaka (Ja 26)

Godhajātaka 03. (Ja 325). The story of the past is very similar to No.1 above, except that there is only mention of one ascetic and he is a hypocrite. The young lizard threatened to expose the ascetic’s hypocrisy and compelled him to leave the hermitage. The story was related in reference to a monk who was a cheat and a rogue (Ja.iii.84f). Cf. the Kuhaka Brāhmaṇavatthu (Dhp-a.iv.154f.).

Godhajātaka 04. (Ja 333). A prince and his wife, returning after a long journey, were greatly distressed by hunger, and some hunters, seeing them, gave them a roasted lizard. The wife carried it in her hand, hanging it from a creeper. Arriving at a lake, they sat down at the foot of a tree, and while his wife was away fetching water the prince ate the whole lizard. When his wife came back, he told her that the lizard had run away, leaving only the tail in his hand. Later, the prince became king, but his wife, though appointed queen consort, received no real honour. The Bodhisatta, who was the king’s minister, wishing to see justice done to the queen, contrived that the king should be reminded of his ingratitude by allusion being made to the incident of the roast lizard. The king thereupon realised his neglect of his dutiful wife, and conferred on her supreme power.

The story was told in reference to a couple who had been given a roast lizard, when returning from a journey undertaken to collect debts. The husband ate the whole lizard when his wife was away. She said nothing and drank some water to appease her hunger, but when they visited the Buddha, and he asked her if her husband were good and affectionate, she replied in the negative. The Buddha then told her the story of the past. Ja.iii.106f.; cf. Succajajātaka.
